title: Mooregate redevelopment stays postponed; housing plan and youth data reviewed
subtitle: Committee also received reports on the 10-year housing plan, homelessness data and youth priorities.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended continuing the postponement of the Waterloo Region Housing redevelopment at 15-105 Mooregate Crescent in Kitchener {{vote:m2}}. Staff said cost consultants found no scenario feasible in the current market without a significant capital contribution from the Region. The committee also recommended that staff develop an expression of interest framework for non-profits and co-operatives for the remaining revitalization projects, and pursue external funding. Council will consider these recommendations later.

For residents, this means the Mooregate site stays vacant while staff explore partners. Tenants were relocated, mostly to other Waterloo Region Housing properties, and about 11,500 households are on the centralized housing waitlist.

The committee received, for information, reports on the 10 Year Housing and Homelessness Plan update, a new approach to homelessness data, and youth priorities from the Children and Youth Planning Table. The housing plan must go to the Province by the end of May. A councillor said a notice of motion on a municipal housing corporation would go to the April 22 Council meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended continuing to postpone the Mooregate Crescent redevelopment in Kitchener {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended that staff develop an expression of interest framework for non-profits and co-operatives for the remaining Waterloo Region Housing revitalization projects.
The committee recommended that staff pursue external funding to advance the Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan.

debate: Councillors expressed concern for Mooregate's relocated tenants, who have been out of the site for years. Staff said all were relocated, mostly to other Waterloo Region Housing properties, and that communication would continue.

One councillor urged staff to move quickly to identify partners and to report back to keep the process accountable. Staff said the work is a priority but must follow procurement and legal requirements, and the project cannot add debt servicing the Region cannot afford.

On the 10 Year Housing and Homelessness Plan, councillors asked that the submission to the Province set out the full funding need. Staff said it would show total need, the split of federal, provincial and municipal investment, and the remaining gap.
Councillors raised hidden homelessness among women. Staff said it is hard to count and likely always under-reported, and one councillor said some women avoid shelters for safety.

On the youth report, one councillor asked why mental health and addictions were not among the six priorities. Delegates said these issues ranked lower among respondents up to age 18, and that the priorities target root causes such as housing, access to family doctors and bullying in schools.
